extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR units, facility compliance staff, State environmental permit program staff, and regulatory counsel/stakeholders
extracted.subtask_short: CCR document retention and state permits
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and retention/posting timeframes for documents related to Coal Combustion Residuals (CCR) units, plus guidance on State CCR permit program approval, RIA findings, and Paperwork Reduction Act (ICR) handling. Focused on ensuring public availability of records and State/Federal permit implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduce destroyed/discarded documents in operating record and repost on facility website
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents destroyed or discarded must be reproduced and placed in the operating record and reposted on the facility website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA believes allowing inconsistency across facility websites (dependent on whether a facility elected to remove documents from the website and operating record and not otherwise retain them) is unacceptable; reproduction and reposting prevents inconsistencies and ensures information is publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents remain available for a reasonable period after milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents must remain available for a reasonable time period after related milestones are reached (e.g., completion of closure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For many documents, EPA has chosen five years as the reasonable time period for document posting and retention after work is completed or the unit's status changes; this aligns with timeframes suggested by commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: State approved CCR program continues to operate in lieu of Federal portions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State has an approved program pursuant to RCRA section 4005(d), that State program will continue to operate in lieu of the portions of the Federal program adopted by the State, even if EPA revised the Federal analog of that regulation in this final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable revisions to the Federal CCR regulations will only take effect in an approved State when the State revises its program to adopt them.

rubrics_metrics.name: State must revise program within three years to maintain approval (42 U.S.C. 6945(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: RCRA requires a State to revise its program within three years of any applicable revision to the Federal CCR regulation that is more protective than the existing State program in order to maintain approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal requirements apply in nonparticipating or partial-approval States
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal requirements continue to apply directly to CCR facilities in States without an approved CCR program and in States with a partial CCR program.

rubrics_metrics.name: States must update regulations and seek approval to permit new unit types
rubrics_metrics.description: Because legacy CCR surface impoundments and CCRMU are new Federally regulated units, any State that wants approval to issue permits to such units will be required to update the State CCR regulations and go through the State CCR permit program approval process set forth in RCRA section 4005(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: States may seek partial approval and adopt only some provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance Document (Interim Final) contemplates a State requesting partial approval of a State CCR permit program; a State may request approval of final rule provisions applicable to either or both legacy CCR surface impoundments and CCRMU.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States can adopt regulations for either legacy CCR surface impoundments or CCRMU, but not necessarily both, via partial program approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA review timeline for complete State program submission — 180 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the State has a complete and approvable program, EPA will issue the final program determination within 180 days of determining that the State's submission is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will work with States to review draft application materials and provide comments to help ensure timely approval; process for program modifications is the same as initial approval (propose to approve/deny, hold public hearing during comment period, then final determination within 180 days of completeness).

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA will establish Federal CCR permits where States do not adopt provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State chooses not to adopt certain portions of this final rule, when EPA establishes a Federal CCR permit program, EPA will begin issuing permits for CCR units, legacy CCR surface impoundments, and CCRMU in nonparticipating States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-implementing rule remains in effect until State or Federal permit obtained
rubrics_metrics.description: All owners and operators of CCR units and CCRMU will need to follow the self-implementing rule until they obtain a State or Federal permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA disagrees that the self-implementing rule is inappropriate in lieu of WIIN Act requirements because it remains applicable until permitting occurs; any permits issued by EPA will refer to 40 CFR part 257, subpart D or equivalent State regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA: define affected universe categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The universe of facilities and units affected includes: (1) facilities with legacy CCR surface impoundments (RIA identifies 194 impoundments at 84 facilities), (2) CCRMU (195 CCRMU at 104 facilities), (3) CCRMU at other active facilities (15 OAFUs at 6 facilities), and (4) CCR landfills already regulated but with waste in contact with groundwater (39 landfills at 33 facilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by EPA to estimate costs and benefits of the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA baseline assumption: existing corrective actions reduce incremental costs
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent legacy CCR surface impoundments and CCRMU are already addressing contamination (baseline), they are assumed not to incur costs or realize benefits under the final rule; EPA estimated ~9.8% of legacy impoundments and ~20.8% of CCRMU are addressing contamination in the baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA cost estimates and cost categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Annualized costs estimated at approximately $214-$240 million/year (2% discount); broken down by unit type and include costs for unit closure, corrective action, fugitive dust controls, structural integrity inspections, and recordkeeping and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: RIA monetized benefits and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Annualized monetized benefits estimated at approximately $53-$80 million/year (2% discount) across unit types; monetized benefits in the RIA are incomplete and omit important categories (e.g., some avoided cancer benefits tied to draft IRIS arsenic values are only in sensitivity analyses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RIA also discusses unquantified/ non-monetized benefits (e.g., avoided leakage/failures due to climate-driven severe weather, various health endpoints lacking dose-response data, ecosystem benefits, avoided drinking water treatment costs, property value improvements, land reuse).

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA establishes requirements under RCRA sections without regard to cost
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA establishes the requirements under RCRA sections 1008(a)(3) and 4004(a) without taking cost into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA indicates it designed the proposal based on statutory factors and court precedent and did not rely on the benefit-cost analysis to select the proposed alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12866/14904 significant regulatory action and OMB review
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is a 'significant regulatory action' under Executive Order 12866 (as amended by EO 14094); EPA submitted the action to OMB for review and documented any changes made in response to recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA prepared the Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) summarized in Unit V and made it available in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) — submit ICR to OMB and public comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collection activities in this rule will be submitted for approval to OMB under the PRA. EPA submitted the proposed rule ICR to OMB on March 25, 2024, triggering a 30-day public comment period for this proposed information collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final ICR anticipated to be approved by the effective date of the rule; if EPA receives new substantive comments on the proposed collection (those not received during earlier 60-day comment period), EPA will address them in an ICR revision via standard PRA approval process.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICR control number handling and merging into existing ICR
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is requesting a temporary OMB control number for this rulemaking collection, to be assigned upon OMB approval of the proposed ICR. EPA will submit a request to merge this rulemaking collection into the existing ICR for the program (2050-0223) once the final rulemaking ICR and renewal for 2050-0223 are approved by OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The information collection requirements are not enforceable until OMB approves them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy CCR surface impoundments must comply with existing reporting/recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule requires legacy CCR surface impoundments to comply with the reporting and recordkeeping requirements already in place for regulated CCR units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many of these requirements are one-time requirements occurring soon after promulgation; several are ongoing.
